instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a "lobbyist" as an individual employed by a principal or who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses," with no dollar threshold — any paid lobbying activity qualifies.

The lobbyist definition turns on receiving economic consideration from a principal, not on the lobbyist's own expenditures; no expenditure-based threshold for lobbyist definition appears in the statute.

Individual itemized disclosure of payments to a lobbyist is required only if the total to that lobbyist "exceeds $200 during the reporting period," meaning individual expenditures below that need not be itemized (Tier −1).

A principal whose lobbying expenditures/obligations do not exceed $500 in a calendar year may file only a verified statement and is exempt from licensing, registration, and expense-reporting requirements.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The statute contains no percentage-of-compensated-time de minimis exemption for a lobbyist's own filing obligation; §13.68(1)(a) provides only an hours-based (10 hours per reporting period) carve-out for non-lobbyist employees from the principal's aggregate reporting, which is not a lobbyist-side percent-of-time exemption.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell based on the Wisconsin statute text.

**row_001**: The definition of "lobbyist" in §13.62(11) requires receiving "economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses" — no dollar threshold for the lobbyist definition itself. The threshold ($500) applies to the principal's registration obligation, not lobbyist definition. So any compensated lobbyist must register — threshold is effectively $0.

**row_002**: No expenditure threshold on the lobbyist side for definition; lobbyist is defined by being employed/compensated, not by their own spending.

**row_003**: §13.62(11) — "If an individual's duties on behalf of a principal are not limited exclusively to lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period."

**row_004**: §13.68(1)(a) requires aggregate total reporting; §13.68(1)(a)5 has a $500 threshold for paid advertising/grassroots; §13.68(1)(a)6 requires itemizing lobbyist payments only if exceeding $200.

**row_005**: §13.621(5) — principals anticipating expenditures not exceeding $500/calendar year may file verified statement and avoid full registration/reporting; §13.64(1) registration only triggered when exceeding $500.

**row_006**: §13.68(1)(a) excludes from aggregate reporting "any employee of the principal who is not a lobbyist and who devotes not more than 10 hours to lobbying during a reporting period" — this is hours, not a percentage. No percentage-of-compensated-time exemption appears for the lobbyist's own filing.
